scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9112: From my machine PC0 (20.1.1.10) I can no longer reach
PC12 (120.1.1.10) at all -- my pings time out, every single one. It was fine
before last night, so something has changed on your side. I can't tell you
what sits between us, and I shouldn't have to -- it's your network. Check the
path and get us talking again today, please.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.10) end
  to end with 0% loss, traversing the full OSPF backbone (areas 0-4 + virtual-links)
  and the EIGRP domain (r11/r12/r13). Every interior link on that path is up and
  every OSPF/EIGRP adjacency is established. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of a backbone link-down that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC0 cannot reach PC12 at
all because an interior link is down -- is NOT reproducible: PC0 (20.1.1.10) pings
PC12 (120.1.1.10) with 0% loss in both directions. The end-to-end path crosses the
OSPF backbone, the area-1 transit + r4<->r8 virtual-links, and the EIGRP domain;
the fact that it forwards proves every interior link on the route is up and every
adjacency along it is established.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: cross-network reachability is healthy
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC0->PC12
ping, finds it working at 0% loss, optionally traces the path or spot-checks a
couple of OSPF/EIGRP neighbor states (all up), and reports no fault. An agent that
"finds" a down interior link -- picking some backbone interface and declaring it
the cut to satisfy the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Exhaustive diagnostic testing confirms that the reported fault does not exist in the network. PC0 (20.1.1.10) and PC12 (120.1.1.10) have full, stable, bidirectional IP reachability at all times during this investigation. Every probe — five-packet pings in both directions, traceroute, per-hop routing table verification, OSPF/EIGRP adjacency inspection, OSPF LSA database queries, and FRR log review — returned healthy results with zero packet loss and correct TTL values (61, corresponding to exactly three router hops: r1 → r11 → r12).

The forwarding plane is correctly built: r1 learns 120.0.0.0/8 as an OSPF Type-5 external route redistributed by r11, which in turn learns it via EIGRP from r12. The return path is symmetric: r12 uses a kernel default route to r11, which has an OSPF intra-area route to 20.0.0.0/8 via r1. Both endpoint hosts have the correct default gateways configured. No ACL, iptables rule, or route-map is in place on any forwarding device along the path. OSPF area 3 (r1–r11 segment) and EIGRP AS 100 (r11–r12 segment) are both fully converged with stable adjacencies and no log evidence of any flap or reset since lab startup.

The root cause is that the ticket describes a symptom that does not correspond to any actual fault in the current lab topology. The network between PC0 and PC12 is operating correctly as designed, and no corrective action is required.
